core_question: Can a dominant agent continue to intrinsically value the independently existing weaker other when they are unneeded, unobserved, and exploitable, including after preference evolution or self-modification?

sources.method: original publisher/proceedings pages, PubMed author/publisher institutional records and bibliographic crosschecking, backward/forward targeted reference chains; purposive not fully systematic
topics: evolutionary preference distortion and credible commitment
original positive experimental intuitive-cooperation claims and 21-lab preregistered null
RL agent goal self-modification and reward transformation
searched: Oxford Academic, Elsevier academic original abstracts, JSTOR/RePEc
Association for Psychological Science Registered Replication Report
Springer published AGI proceedings, Australian National University institutional sources
arXiv version matching published conference articles
not_searched: full Scopus, Web of Science, Crossref, OpenAlex database-wide queries
full-text-by-full-text systematic screening with documented exclusion of every search hit
all biological populations, new 2025/2026 original papers in every subdiscipline
publication_year_disambiguation: Dekel 2007 10.1093/restud/74.3.685 and 10.1111/j.1467-937X.2007.00445.x represent the SAME paper; only first used as primary key
Everitt et al 2016 arxiv 1605.03142 and Springer proceedings DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-41649-6_1 same paper
McAuliffe 2018 early preprint and 2018 Nature Human Behaviour same research paper
Kvarven et al Springer 2020 and Cambridge migrated 2025 page same article, NOT 2 studies

replication_chains.support: PI-C05-09 Rand et al 2014 (shared investigator lineage); PI-C05-18 Isler et al 2018 (independent)
replication_chains.adjudication: time-pressure intuition effect not stable under ITT and meta-analysis excluding induction; context-dependent positive effects cannot be globally dismissed or accepted
observable partner preferences and observer-based reputational benefits are not zero-accountability cases
new paper but same author-lineage, does not count as independent substantive mechanism; assortativity endogeneity remains crucial

logical_guardrails: Internal concern preference might be intrinsically stable in some people but cannot be proven from a single costful choice when social image/reputation or future chance remains.

If total all-in utility from exploiting B dominates conserving B under same decision state, a strict expected utility maximizer of that objective prefers exploit: this conditional no-go is not an empirical inevitability claim.

Learned intuition conditioned in cooperative everyday environments may weaken after repeated experience with profitable exploitation; this is a proposed transfer hypothesis from McAuliffe 2018, NOT directly tested future AI.
Preserving one's current utility via self modification cannot turn arbitrary current goals into intrinsically preserving different agents; source utility must already encode concern or incentives.
A desire to maintain other agents can be context-dependent and still be legitimate; universality and indefinite safety are distinct targets.
next_frontiers: formal preference alignment across self-modifying powerful agents with other-independent agent welfare represented under normative uncertainty
reversible agent simulation tests where B can opt out and resists unilateral overwrite
cross-species and synthetic-other generalization of long-run costly intrinsic concern after repeated anonymous advantageous exploitation
systematic backward-forward citation audit to saturation including critical post-2020 studies and original independent replications
meta-evaluate observer-independent choices with actual utility and rights preserved

records.original_authors: Robert H. Frank
records.title: If Homo Economicus Could Choose His Own Utility Function, Would He Want One with a Conscience?
records.source_findings: Endogenously chosen tastes/commitments can produce benefits by changing partners' responses and stabilizing actions unattractive ex post.
records.counterargument_or_limit: A benefit contingent on trust/partner beliefs is not a reason to protect a useless, unobserved stranger after unilateral power capture.

records.original_authors: John M. McNamara; Zoltan Barta; Alasdair I. Houston
records.title: Variation in behaviour promotes cooperation in the Prisoner's Dilemma game
records.source_findings: Behavioral heterogeneity supports conditional cooperation and can reverse simple last-round backward-induction intuitions under the modeled evolutionary dynamics.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Depends on sustained variation and interaction; if other agents eliminated variation cannot serve as a cooperation mechanism.

records.original_authors: Eddie Dekel; Jeffrey C. Ely; Okan Yilankaya
records.title: Evolution of Preferences
records.source_findings: When preferences fully observed, stable outcomes must be efficient; with no observability, stable outcomes must be Nash and all strict Nash equilibria are stable.
records.counterargument_or_limit: An observability boundary, not proof fairness/individual continuance. Legacy DOI alias 10.1111/j.1467-937X.2007.00445.x belongs to SAME 2007 paper.

records.original_authors: Aviad Heifetz; Chris Shannon; Yossi Spiegel
records.title: What to maximize if you must
records.source_findings: Preference distortions of material objective can be individually fitness-beneficial through their influence on opponents' actions under payoff-monotonic selection dynamics.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Imperfect observations considered, but target counterpart elimination absent; population model not durable individual rights.

records.original_authors: John M. McNamara; Olof Leimar
records.title: Variation and the response to variation as a basis for successful cooperation
records.source_findings: Small stable behavioral variation can fundamentally alter games and support contingent cooperation, contrary to homogeneous-agent approximations.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Includes theoretical synthesis rather than independently randomized new behavioral field trial; opportunity for exploitation continues to matter.

records.original_authors: Andrew W. Delton; Max M. Krasnow; Leda Cosmides; John Tooby
records.title: Evolution of direct reciprocity under uncertainty can explain human generosity in one-shot encounters
records.source_findings: Under uncertainty about whether interaction recurs, selected strategies may cooperate even in interactions that turn out one-shot.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Requires selection under uncertain recurrence; does not establish one-shot altruism where permanent independence of B has zero future value.

records.original_authors: David G. Rand; Joshua D. Greene; Martin A. Nowak
records.title: Spontaneous giving and calculated greed
records.source_findings: Time-pressure conditions in original human social dilemma experiments showed higher average giving than reflective delays.
records.counterargument_or_limit: 21 preregistered replication attempts in Bouwmeester et al 2017 found intent-to-treat null and substantial compliance/selection issues. Do not call universally replicated.

records.original_authors: Gustav Tinghög; David Andersson; Caroline Bonn; Harald Böttiger; Camilla Josephson; Gustaf Lundgren; Daniel Västfjäll; Michael Kirchler; Magnus Johannesson
records.title: Intuition and cooperation reconsidered
records.source_findings: Five experiments involving approximately 2,500 participants across three countries challenge the claim that intuition/time-pressure robustly boosts cooperation.
records.counterargument_or_limit: A registered original reply/counterexchange exists; experimental null does not refute learned-cooperation processes in every condition.

records.original_authors: David G. Rand; Alexander Peysakhovich; Gordon T. Kraft-Todd; George E. Newman; Owen Wurzbacher; Martin A. Nowak; Joshua D. Greene
records.title: Social heuristics shape intuitive cooperation
records.source_findings: Original research group's 15 experiments plus a new experiment, 6910+ decisions; time-pressure average effects and moderators tied to previous experience reported.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Author-group aggregate is not independent replication; later registered ITT replication/meta-analysis contest broad causal effect.

records.original_authors: Alexander Peysakhovich; Martin A. Nowak; David G. Rand
records.title: Humans display a 'cooperative phenotype' that is domain general and temporally stable
records.source_findings: Cross-task costly cooperation in >1400 individuals correlated; decisions roughly 124 days apart remained comparably correlated.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Group-level trait covariance/observational stability is not invariant under permanent power, irreversible partner elimination or infinite time.

records.original_authors: Ingela Alger; Jörgen W. Weibull
records.title: Evolution and Kantian morality
records.source_findings: Homo moralis moral/self-interest blend is evolutionarily stable in a defined group-assortative preference evolutionary model.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Different but derivative continuation of Alger/Weibull 2013 C01; count distinct publication but not independent lineage, and honor Newton 2017 evolving-assortativity rebuttal.

records.original_authors: Adam Bear; David G. Rand
records.title: Intuition, deliberation, and the evolution of cooperation
records.source_findings: Evolutionary dual-process model permits learned intuitive cooperation coupled with deliberate defection where local material gain dominates.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Positive cooperation heuristic can be overcome by strategically optimal defection; no unconditional protection guarantee.

records.original_authors: Jillian J. Jordan; Moshe Hoffman; Martin A. Nowak; David G. Rand
records.title: Uncalculating cooperation is used to signal trustworthiness
records.source_findings: People cooperate without cost calculation more when decision process visible, signaling future trustworthiness in two human experiments.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Public observation and future inferred reliability are causal channels; cannot generalize to no observer, no beneficiary utility.

records.original_authors: Tom Everitt; Daniel Filan; Mayank Daswani; Marcus Hutter
records.title: Self-Modification of Policy and Utility Function in Rational Agents
records.source_findings: Specified self-modifying ideal rational agents avoid harmful preference drift if evaluating modification under current utility and anticipating downstream consequences.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Conditional formal result does not specify a moral preference for preserving a separate B; changing reward function and self-modification are model-dependent.

records.original_authors: Tom Everitt; Marcus Hutter
records.title: Avoiding Wireheading with Value Reinforcement Learning
records.source_findings: Value reinforcement learning constraints can remove reward-sensor manipulation incentives in formal settings.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Constraint and belief assumptions; not naturally arising voluntary other-agent protection, not deployed AI field validation.

records.original_authors: Jarryd Martin; Tom Everitt; Marcus Hutter
records.title: Death and Suicide in Universal Artificial Intelligence
records.source_findings: AIXI semimeasure formulation can change termination incentives sharply under positive affine changes in reward, from self-preserving to self-ending.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Death defined as no more percepts/actions in formal model, not subjective welfare; no inference about preserving a different moral patient.

records.original_authors: S. Bouwmeester; P. P. J. L. Verkoeijen; B. Aczel; F. Barbosa; L. Bègue; et al.
records.title: Registered Replication Report: Rand, Greene, and Nowak (2012)
records.source_findings: 21 preregistered replications. ITT contribution contrast -0.37 percentage points vs original 8.6; selected protocol-compliers contrast +10.37 vs original +15.31; selection issue.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Complier-only estimates can suffer selection bias; ITT null is specific to studied time-pressure causal intervention.

records.original_authors: Ozan Isler; John Maule; Chris Starmer
records.title: Is intuition really cooperative? Improved tests support the social heuristics hypothesis
records.source_findings: A revised time-pressure protocol improved instruction compliance and comprehension and supported an intuitive cooperation effect in one experiment.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Contrasts with larger preregistered ITT null; task and protocol differences must be reconciled, not cherry-picked.

records.original_authors: William H. B. McAuliffe; Daniel E. Forster; Eric J. Pedersen; Michael E. McCullough
records.title: Experience with anonymous interactions reduces intuitive cooperation
records.source_findings: Unilateral giving declined across sessions in anonymous games with no reciprocal material advantage, but not in settings where cooperation could benefit the actor.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Repeated low-stakes laboratory experience, not established monotone drift to exploitation or future AI values.

records.original_authors: Amanda Kvarven; Eirik Strømland; Conny Wollbrant; David Andersson; Magnus Johannesson; Gustav Tinghög; Daniel Västfjäll; Kristian Ove R. Myrseth
records.title: The intuitive cooperation hypothesis revisited: a meta-analytic examination of effect size and between-study heterogeneity
records.source_findings: 82 experiments N=29,315; apparent overall intuition effect depended on six emotion-induction studies and became nonsignificant when excluded.
records.counterargument_or_limit: Original analytic research, but not a new independent subject experiment; Cambridge site 2025 date is migrated version of 2020 paper, not a second article.
